sourceRef: https://www.sars.gov.za/wp-content/uploads/Ops/Guides/PAYE-GEN-01-G21-Guide-for-Employers-iro-Employees-Tax-for-2027-External-Guide.pdf ; SARS e@syFile Employer Reconciliation BRS (SARS_PAYE_BRS V25.3.0, Jun-26)
notes: R400 000 determined value, no maintenance plan: 3.5% = R14 000 a month (G21 p. 5). Employer-provided vehicle with business use below 80%: 80% of the benefit is remuneration for PAYE = R11 200 (BRS code 4582 p. 105: "The portion (80 or 20%) of the allowance and benefit which is subject to PAYE", listing 3802). Taxable remuneration 40 000 + 11 200 = 51 200; x12 = 614 400; tax = 125 599 + 36% x (614 400 - 530 200) = 155 911; less the R17 820 rebate = 138 091; /12 = 11507.58. Before wave 5 FB the calculator taxed the full R14 000 benefit as cash (the gap this case closed). NAMED LIMIT: the G21 text states the 80/20 rule only for the travel allowance (p. 5); for the vehicle benefit it is the BRS code 4582 description plus Seventh Schedule para 7 / Fourth Schedule para 9(1) (not fetched): MEDIUM confidence on the 80%. UIF is not flagged on the benefit and employee UIF is at the R177.12 ceiling either way; SDL is derived below. The 3802 amount is the full benefit (the IRP5 figure). SDL AND NET ADDED (FB review round 2): SDL: the SDL-flagged 3802 counts at its PAYE share (SDL Act s3; Fourth Schedule para 1; G21 p. 5): 1% x R51 200 = R512.00. Net = R40 000 cash (the vehicle is non-cash) - PAYE 11 507.58 - UIF 177.12 = R28315.30; the benefit is non-cash, so it is in neither gross nor net pay. These two figures are derived from the cited rules and the sourced PAYE and UIF, not read from a payslip.
